slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Azure Virtual Desktop earns its place in specific situations, and it is worth being clear about which. It is excellent when you need people working on company systems from equipment you do not control, so contractors, offshore teams, personal machines and anyone using their own laptop. It keeps the data in Azure rather than on the endpoint, which is a genuine security win. It suits a legacy application that refuses to behave on modern desktops. It is also the fastest way to onboard twenty people at once without waiting on hardware.

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: It is not automatically cheaper than buying laptops. Session hosts are virtual machines and they bill while they run, so the cost case depends entirely on sizing them properly and letting autoscale shut capacity down outside working hours. Get that wrong and you have bought an expensive way to run Windows. Profiles matter too, because user data has to live somewhere sensible or logins slow to a crawl, which is what FSLogix profile containers are for.

slots.label: Paragraph 7
slots.default: If you already have Microsoft 365 Business Premium or a Windows E3 or E5 plan, the desktop entitlement is typically already included, so you are paying Azure for the compute and storage rather than buying a whole new product. We will work out whether the numbers land in your favour before recommending it, and say so if they do not.
